clue.text: Cramped hippo, see, needs appliance that's flexible

indicators.note: cramped suggests letters squeezed and pushed out of shape, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hippo squashed into a tight space needs some bendy equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cramped' is the anagram signal: the letters of HIPPO and SEE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hose is a flexible tube used as an appliance for watering.

clue.text: Entertainer offers great numbers

definitions.meaning: one who receives and entertains guests
a multitude, as in a ... of admirers

explanation.surface: A performer provides plenty of songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a person entertaining guests and a large crowd are standard senses of the same word.

clue.text: Advances when transport turns up from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Progress comes when a vehicle arrives from the southern direction.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turns up' reads the vehicle from the bottom upwards; 'Advances' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Subs are informal advance payments on wages, as in asking for a sub until payday.

clue.text: Some gaped at earthlings with feet

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Aliens stare open-mouthed at humans walking on legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedate is a zoological and botanical term for having feet or foot-like divisions.

clue.text: Having moved pepper pot, aunt began to write

indicators.note: the pepper pot and the aunt are shifted about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aunt shifts the cruet on the table and then starts writing a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having moved' is the anagram signal over the letters of PEPPER POT and AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for starting to compose something in writing is to set pen to paper.

clue.text: Brownie in snap has a hang-up

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun, someone who has an irrational fear

indicators.note: in places the goblin's name inside the word for a photograph

parts.note: a snap is a photo, informally a pic
a hob is a sprite or brownie of folklore

explanation.surface: A young Girl Guide in a photograph seems troubled about something.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brownie is a junior Girl Guide in the surface, but here it is a household goblin of folklore, placed 'in' the photo.
explanation.definitionFit: A phobic is a person with an irrational fear, the kind of fixation called a psychological hang-up.

clue.text: Prince accepts I live with sailors of a winter

indicators.note: accepts means the prince's name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
to live is to be
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A prince lets a narrator move in alongside navy men for the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' wraps Shakespeare's Prince around the rest; RN, the Royal Navy, is a standard crossword shorthand for sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernal is the Latin-derived adjective meaning wintry or belonging to the cold season.

clue.text: John Lawrence, in spring, gets the dog

indicators.note: in places the two names inside the word for a leap

parts.note: to spring is to bound
john is slang for a toilet, a loo
D H Lawrence, the novelist

explanation.surface: A man named John Lawrence acquires a pet in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: John Lawrence looks like one person's name, but John is slang for a toilet and Lawrence is the novelist D H Lawrence; 'in' puts both inside the leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloodhound is a large scent-tracking breed of hound.

clue.text: Inside spread little money about for congregation

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
re means about or concerning
a fold is a flock of the faithful, a church congregation

explanation.surface: A small donation is passed round among the worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrefold is the double-page spread in the middle of a magazine.

clue.text: Press person to get hopeful lover in bed? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary flips the stated arrangement, so the bed goes in the lover rather than the lover in bed

parts.note: a suitor hopes to win the one he courts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A journalist tries to get a would-be romeo between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads lover in bed; 'On the contrary' swaps container and contents, so the bed goes inside the lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor works for the press, checking and correcting copy for a newspaper.

clue.text: Unexpectedly reprieve Scott exhibition

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Scott is suddenly let off the hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' is the anagram signal over the letters of REPRIEVE and SCOTT.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrospective is an exhibition surveying the work of an artist across their career.

clue.text: Wife taken in by Eleanor's colour

indicators.note: taken in by means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: Eleanor Bron is an English actress

explanation.surface: A married woman is fooled by Eleanor's choice of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' looks like being deceived, but W goes inside BRON, the surname of actress Eleanor Bron.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown is a colour, the shade of earth or wood.

clue.text: Barrow boy with red setter, tar-spattered

indicators.note: spattered means splashed about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A market seller has a red setter dog covered in tar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spattered' is the anagram signal over RED SETTER and TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow boy sells goods from a cart in the street, a British term for a street vendor.

clue.text: Quiet: nothing to inspect during drive for three blessed days!

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: during means one piece falls within the other

parts.note: a ride or drive is a journey in a vehicle
O looks like zero, nothing
to vet is to inspect

explanation.surface: Hush: there is nothing to check on a car outing for a holy festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' sets the zero and the check inside the drive; Shrovetide ends on Shrove Tuesday, pancake day.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrovetide is the three days before Ash Wednesday, when Christians went to be shriven of sins.

clue.text: Retainer may, ludicrously, be all straw

indicators.note: ludicrously means absurdly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something holding things back may absurdly be made of straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ludicrously' is the anagram signal over BE ALL STRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A breast wall is a retaining wall built against a bank of earth to hold it back.

clue.text: Listen to hospital ship

parts.note: Noah's ark was a ship

explanation.surface: Pay attention to a hospital vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hark is an old imperative meaning to listen or pay attention.

clue.text: Meat cooked thus, scraps of horse sent back, bad

indicators.note: sent back means each of the words before it is reversed

parts.note: orts are scraps of leftover food
a nag is a horse
food gone off is bad

explanation.surface: Meat prepared this way, with leftover horse returned to the kitchen as inedible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns each of the two words for scraps and horse, giving STRO and GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroganoff is a dish of strips of meat cooked in a sour cream sauce.

clue.text: Artist introduced to lively rag by man of the land

indicators.note: introduced to means the artist is set within the other letters
lively suggests letters bouncing into a fresh order

parts.note: Ian is a man's name
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is shown a jolly ragtime tune played by a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lively' rearranges the rag to AGR; 'introduced to' sets the Royal Academician between that and the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian describes things relating to farmland and cultivation.

clue.text: Fruit seeds produced by Spiro Agnew (the last to be dropped for President)

indicators.note: produced by suggests the letters are reworked to make something new

indicators.text: the last to be dropped for
indicators.note: the final letter of the name is removed and replaced by the next piece

explanation.surface: Spiro Agnew, a vice-president, is credited with some pips, minus Bush as president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last to be dropped for' swaps the final W of AGNEW for P, then 'produced by' rearranges SPIROAGNEP. W is also a nickname for President Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Pips are small seeds, such as those found in citrus fruit.

clue.text: Indigo gets a zero

parts.note: nil means zero

explanation.surface: A deep blue earns a score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it.

clue.text: Note in tender profession

indicators.note: in places the musical note inside the word for one who tends

parts.note: one who tends or looks after someone is a carer
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A banknote offered as payment for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' reads like money offered, but it is a CARER, one who tends; the note E goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is one's chosen profession or line of work.

clue.text: Additional policeman is unusually distinguished

parts.note: extra means additional
a special is a special constable, a volunteer police officer in Britain

explanation.surface: Another officer turns out to be exceptionally notable.
explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a part-time volunteer British police officer, often just called a special.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra-special means exceptionally fine or distinguished beyond the ordinary.

clue.text: Foreshortened sketch appeared

indicators.note: foreshortened says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a cameo is a short descriptive sketch

explanation.surface: A drawing with compressed perspective became visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreshortened' removes the last letter of CAMEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Came means arrived or showed up, appeared.

clue.text: Indeed, doesn't everyone say their leaders make this a prophetic day?

indicators.note: the leaders of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Doesn't the whole world agree that this date was foretold?
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides of March was the day the soothsayer warned Julius Caesar of in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides of March is remembered for a soothsayer's prophecy of Caesar's death.

clue.text: One of the Gershwins to question one from the Middle East

parts.note: Ira Gershwin wrote lyrics for his brother George
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Gershwin brother is set to interrogate someone from the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraqi describes a person or thing from Iraq, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Right back is full of dash in Germany

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a place found in Germany

indicators.note: is full of means the word for back contains the next piece

parts.note: hind means back or rear
elan is dash or flair

explanation.surface: A football right-back plays with flair in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right back' looks like a football position, but it is two pieces; 'is full of' puts the dash inside the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhineland is a region of western Germany along the river Rhine.

clue.text: Don't start therapeutic comedies here, not now!

indicators.note: don't start means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: healing means curative, therapeutic

explanation.surface: Someone told not to begin on curative comedies, which are a thing of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' removes the H of HEALING. Ealing Studios in west London made the famous Ealing comedies of the 1940s and 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing Studios produced a celebrated run of British film comedies, no longer made.

clue.text: Hard to go back round Provençal town without crying

indicators.note: round means the reversed word wraps around the town
go back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: set means hardened, as concrete sets hard
Arles is a town in Provence, southern France

explanation.surface: It is difficult to return to a southern French town without weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go back' turns the word for hard into TES, which goes 'round' the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearless means dry-eyed, without weeping.
